items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: So and Jean, she understood, too. She had had a private talk with him while I was home one day.

ctx.x: Now, afterwards, it came to me. He called me and took me over to St. Luke's Hospital. When he told me to go with him, I used common sense. He was my doctor. And as long as I was with him, I wouldn't do anything wrong. So and Jean, she understood, too. She had had a private talk with him while I was home one day. She went up there to get me some medicine. And she understood. So long as I was with Doc, I was all right.

He took me to St. Luke's and on the way, I said, Doctor, did you ever study psychology? It came to me. He put it off, he says, oh, yes, yes, I took it for awhile, but I gave it up, it cost too much money. See, that's what he'd been using on me, psychology, yeah. He was trying to get my thoughts away from my illness, that there were plenty of people worse off than me. And I forgot about it, because I was worried to death I couldn't play.
